classification.difficultyReason: Include the initial height in the vertical equation, then follow the taught elimination and trigonometric-identity procedure and solve a quadratic.

content.prompt:
A ball is thrown from the top of a $15\text{ m}$ tower.

Taking the origin at the base, it is projected at $20\text{ m/s}$ and lands $40\text{ m}$ from the base.

Find the two possible angles to 1 d.p.

answer.worked:
Let $\theta$ be the angle of projection above the horizontal. With the origin at the base and $g=10\text{ m/s}^2$,

$$\begin{aligned}x&=20\cos\theta\,t\\y&=-5t^2+20\sin\theta\,t+15\end{aligned}$$
At landing, $x=40$ and $y=0$.

$$\begin{aligned}40&=20\cos\theta\,t\\t&=\frac{2}{\cos\theta}\end{aligned}$$
Substitute into the vertical equation:

$$\begin{aligned}0&=-5\left(\frac{2}{\cos\theta}\right)^2+20\sin\theta\left(\frac{2}{\cos\theta}\right)+15\\0&=-20\sec^2\theta+40\tan\theta+15\\0&=-20(1+\tan^2\theta)+40\tan\theta+15\\20\tan^2\theta-40\tan\theta+5&=0\\4\tan^2\theta-8\tan\theta+1&=0\\\tan\theta&=\frac{8\pm\sqrt{48}}{8}\\\tan\theta&=1\pm\frac{\sqrt3}{2}\end{aligned}$$
Hence the two possible angles are

$$\theta\approx61.8^\circ\text{ or }7.6^\circ$$
to 1 d.p., both above the horizontal.
